report.summary: Chunk 5 of daedalus/council/bus.py: defines _file_sig, _chain_state, _ends_without_newline, _write_anchor, _chain_records, and append_round (partial).
risks: _chain_state | high | Comment claims 'MUST be called under _WRITE_LOCK' but no enforcement mechanism is visible in this chunk. | Check if callers actually acquire the lock before invoking _chain_state.

_chain_state docstring | medium | Claims 'Any cross-process append changes the size, forcing a reload, so a stale prev can never be bound.' This relies on file size change detection; if another process truncates or overwrites without changing size, the claim could be broken. | Verify that file size is a sufficient signal for detecting all relevant modifications.

append_round docstring | medium | Claims 'Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted by actor id and chained with seq assigned here'. The sorting is not implemented in this chunk; it may be in a later part of append_round not shown. | Check that the missing code does sort by actor id.

append_round docstring | medium | Claims 'Exactly one turn per actor per round is allowed: a duplicate is a caller bug'. No duplicate detection is present in this chunk; it may be in the caller's responsibility or later code. | Verify duplicate handling elsewhere.

_chain_records docstring | high | Claims 'A torn (newline-less) tail is separated with a leading newline'. The implementation uses _ends_without_newline to detect and prefix with '\n'. If another process appends after the check but before the write, the prefix could be incorrect. | Evaluate whether the lock prevents concurrent appends.

_chain_records docstring | medium | Claims 'One chain timestamp for the whole batch: ts is inside entry_sha, so per-turn wall clock would make the head depend on completion order.' This is a design rationale, not a testable claim. | No action needed.
todos: Complete the append_round function: sort by actor id, handle duplicates, and return ids.

handoff.purpose: Internal helpers for appending chained records and the start of public append_round.

symbols.name: _file_sig
symbols.note: Returns (size, mtime_ns) tuple or None if file not found.

symbols.name: _chain_state
symbols.note: Cached state: tail entry_sha, record count, turn count. Uses _APPEND_CACHE and load_transcript.

symbols.name: _ends_without_newline
symbols.note: Checks if last byte of file is not newline.

symbols.name: _write_anchor
symbols.note: Writes anchor JSON file with version, council_id, count, head, ts.

symbols.name: _chain_records
symbols.note: Chains a batch of records and appends to store file under _WRITE_LOCK.

symbols.name: append_round
symbols.note: Public API: chains one round. Normalizes, scans, optionally refuses turns. Incomplete in this chunk.

claims.why: No lock acquisition or assertion is present in _chain_state; the claim refers to caller discipline not enforced here.

claims.text: Any cross-process append changes the size, forcing a reload, so a stale ``prev`` can never be bound.
claims.why: This claim depends on the behavior of _file_sig (which uses stat) and the assumption that any valid cross-process append modifies file size. This chunk does not test that assumption.

claims.text: Tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, cached and invalidated by file signature.
claims.why: The code implements caching via _APPEND_CACHE and invalidates when _file_sig differs from cached sig.

claims.text: A torn (newline-less) tail is separated with a leading newline so this batch lands as its own parseable lines instead of fusing onto the fragment.
claims.why: The code calls _ends_without_newline and prefixes with '\n' if true.

claims.text: Read-then-write happens inside the lock so a concurrent append can neither tear a line nor bind two lines to one ``prev``.
claims.why: The entire append logic is inside the 'with _WRITE_LOCK:' block.

claims.text: One chain timestamp for the whole batch: ``ts`` is inside ``entry_sha``, so per-turn wall clock would make the head depend on completion order.
claims.why: The claim about design rationale is not testable from code alone; the code does use a single ts for the batch.

claims.text: Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted by actor id and chained with ``seq`` assigned here -- so reversed completion order yields a byte-identical chain head.
claims.why: The sorting by actor id is not present in the provided chunk; _normalize_turn and secret-floored are not visible.

claims.text: Exactly one turn per actor per round is allowed: a duplicate is a caller bug that would double a voice, and a missing participant must be recorded as an ``unavailable`` turn rather than skipped.
claims.why: No duplicate detection or enforcement is visible in this chunk; the claim refers to expected caller behavior.

claims.text: The offending bytes never reach the file -- not in the turn, and not in the receipt.
claims.why: The code replaces the turn with a receipt and does not write the original turn, but the actual writing occurs in _chain_records, which is not called in this chunk. The full append_round is incomplete.

observations.what: _chain_state docstring claims it must be called under _WRITE_LOCK, but no enforcement is present.

_ends_without_newline reads last byte of file; if file is empty (sig[0]==0) returns False, but if file has one byte that is a newline, returns True? Actually returns False if sig[0]==0, else reads last byte. If file has exactly one byte that is newline, it returns False (since fh.read(1) == b'\n'), but the function name says 'ends_without_newline', so returning False means it ends with newline. Logic seems correct.
append_round is incomplete; it normalizes and prepares turns but does not sort or chain yet.
_chain_records uses _ends_without_newline after acquiring lock, but another process could append between the check and the write, causing incorrect prefix.
